honest_gaps: BVH is hip-centred: root position channels ~0 (rotation only) — characters flip in place, no root travel or height arc. Panel text says so. A root-motion version would need re-export from landmarks.json world data.

Brief said flip.bvh has 397 frames — the actual export has 513 frames (397 is the count of frames with pose detections). Shipped the real 513-frame file; events at f222/f247/f288/f339 per the study analysis.json.

Brief named Lestya as the face-pipeline subject: the SHIPPED Lestya.glb kept only 2 morph targets (both filtered as explicit one-off shapes) — the Blender face pipeline's ARKit shapes never made that export. Face proof therefore uses Essi (253 morphs, 25 channels driven); Lestya gets the bones-only state (ARP jaw/eyelid bones + head/neck). A morph-bearing Lestya re-export is still owed by the Scarlett/Madelyn-model pipeline, not this lane.

Retarget quality on BlenRig-style rigs: legs thin mid-flip (untwisted skin on twist-bone rigs) and feet are approximate — the flip reads clearly (upright/inverted/landing all verified) but it is a rotation-delta retarget, not a solved IK/mocap-cleanup pass.
Thigh L/R split (1.65/1.47) is display-only: the Jiggle Bones sim consumes one 'thigh' region, so the 1.56 mean is what reaches the sim (noted in the panel readout).

No video file in the showcase: repo .gitignore bans *.mp4 (owner safety rule) — the V5 overlay is replayed from extracted landmark JSON instead of embedding flip-skeleton-overlay.mp4. The rendered overlay clip itself remains in ~/workspace/mocap-flip/ and the proof folder if a future lane wants it hosted elsewhere.

Essi's pale materials render harshly under swiftshader (blown highlights in screenshots) — a software-renderer artifact; her expression delta is still plainly visible between the neutral and smile shots.
